protocol.transport: gloo over shared memory, one host
protocol.grid_construction: log-spaced backbone rounded to 4-byte words, NOT restricted to powers of two, plus oversampling in four named regions

oversampled_regions.name: latency_to_bandwidth
oversampled_regions.why: where the latency floor gives way to a bandwidth slope

oversampled_regions.name: cache_peak
oversampled_regions.why: where effective bandwidth peaked in the previous campaign, consistent with the buffer still fitting in cache

oversampled_regions.name: peak_decline
oversampled_regions.why: where bandwidth fell again past the peak

oversampled_regions.name: prior_breakpoints
oversampled_regions.why: where the earlier two-segment fits placed their breakpoints

protocol.pass_purpose: two independent passes so the bandwidth peak's location, magnitude and regime ordering can be compared; a peak seen once is not a property of the transport
protocol.cross_validation: stratified k-fold over message size, folds assigned round-robin within each regime so no fold can be missing a regime

acceptance.why_not_pooled: a pooled median lets one useless regime hide behind three good ones, which is how a model 35% wrong in the medium tier was previously accepted

a_regime_is_covered_when: it was measured with at least min_points_per_regime valid points
held-out validation graded the model in that regime
the regime's cross-validated error is within the threshold
measurement noise in that regime is within max_noise_cv

protocol.subsystem_readiness: conjunctive: every required group covered, every required regime covered, accepted models only, held-out validation present in every cell. There is no arithmetic that trades a covered group against a missing one.
protocol.transferability: NOTHING measured here is a value for NVLink or InfiniBand. This is gloo over shared memory on one host. What the campaign can establish is methodology readiness -- that the grid, the estimators, the selection rule and the coverage criteria work -- not fabric parameters for an A100 node.

predictions.name: campaign-v2-corrected-gates-v1
predictions.question: With the gradeability gate judging the precision of the point rather than the variability of a call, the block budget following the noise instead of the message size, and structure selected on the same scale the fits use -- does the surface become gradable?

design.held_fixed: the replicate count, so the comparison isolates the harness and gate corrections

corrections_under_test: the timed block is sized by the point's own variability rather than by a 1 MiB threshold, which had put a 4x averaging cliff inside the medium regime
the gradeability gate judges the standard error of the point the model is fitted to, not the population CV of its repeats, which could never respond to measurement effort
a regime that cannot be graded no longer votes to reject a family
breakpoints and segment splits are chosen on relative residuals, the scale all three estimators already use

predictions.claim: The median recorded CV in the medium regime falls by at least a quarter, because points above 1 MiB there averaged 5 calls per timing and will now average considerably more.
predictions.falsified_if: medium-regime CV is unchanged, which would mean the cliff was a coincidence of size rather than of averaging and the harness correction addresses nothing

predictions.claim: The gap between medium points below and above 1 MiB (currently 1.57x) falls below 1.25x, because nothing in the new rule keys on that boundary.
predictions.falsified_if: the gap persists, which would mean something other than the iteration count makes messages above 1 MiB noisier
coverage does not improve, in which case the gates were not what was blocking it and the remaining obstacle is the surface itself

predictions.not_predicted: Nothing here predicts 24 of 24. The corrections are to gates that were measuring the wrong quantity; whether what remains is reachable at all is a separate question, and a result showing the surface is simply too variable in places would be an answer to it.
